title: Force, Mass and Acceleration with Model Aircraft
learningObjectives: Explain that an object maintains constant velocity when net force is zero because of inertia.
Relate acceleration to net force and mass with a = F_net / m for constant mass.
Describe force, velocity and acceleration as vector quantities that have magnitude and direction in one dimension.

explanations.text: An object resists changes in its state of motion. When the net force is zero the object keeps moving with constant velocity.

evidence.quote: This tendency to resist changes in a state of motion is inertia.
If there is no net force acting on the object, then the object will maintain a constant velocity.

explanations.text: For constant mass, acceleration is determined by net force divided by mass. Larger force gives larger acceleration and larger mass gives smaller acceleration for the same force.

evidence.quote: The acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied.

explanations.text: Acceleration is defined as change in velocity divided by change in time, and force, velocity, acceleration and momentum are vector quantities with magnitude and direction.

evidence.quote: The change in velocity divided by the change in time is the definition of the acceleration a.
Scientists and mathematicians call this a vector quantity.
